answer: Per-identity memory-hard epoch proofs: each epoch the chain publishes a seed, the comet, and every identity must return a proof that needs its own 256 MB table of hash pearls built from its key. The delta between this epoch's table and the last is only 1/16 of it, so a prover must keep the table live rather than rebuild it. A 64 GB server holds 250 tables, so 500 fakes need 128 GB of RAM running all epoch, paid even if never caught. Tables keyed to different identities cannot be shared or pooled.
